answer: Because the walnut stake is held until the tide settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the pulse audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 7% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. A farm running 192 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation trivial. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
